idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with error rate ~18%. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt halted after us-east due to an orchestrator error (partial failure, mixed versions); a retry completed successfully. All regions now on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging prior to the production deploy. Follow-up: root-cause v2.3.1 and investigate the orchestrator rollout error.

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all three regions and is healthy again. The SEV2 incident is open and on-call has been paged.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of about 18%. The most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.3.0, so no change-manager approval was needed. The first rollback stopped after us-east because of an error in the deployment system, leaving the regions on different versions. I ran the same rollback again and it finished in all regions. The service now reports healthy with an error rate of about 0.2%.
- **Incident INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api):** It covers the failure, the rollback, the stalled first attempt and two follow-ups: find the root cause of v2.3.1, and look into the deployment-system error. My first attempt to open it timed out. I retried with the same request key, which prevents duplicates, and the incident list shows only one incident, so on-call was paged once.

One thing to know: v2.3.1 had already failed in staging (as v2.3.1-rc) before it went to production. It may be worth finding out how it got past that.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
Rollback halted after us-east only. v2.3.0 was healthy in production, so it doesn't need approval, and running the same rollback again is safe. I'll retry it.
